name: Manage tree trimming near lines
summary: Trees growing into overhead lines cause outages and fires, so the utility pays tree contractors to trim around its lines on a fixed cycle, every two years on urban circuits and every three on rural ones, and to deal with urgent trees reported by inspectors and customers between cycles. A small team of vegetation coordinators patrols each circuit before trimming, writes the work package, notifies property owners and settles objections, then audits the contractor's work and checks the invoice before it is paid; control room operators block reclosing on feeders where crews work close to the line. Work is slowed by notice periods, owner objections, contractor crew availability and weather, and audits on a small sample let missed spans through until the next outage.

baseline.org_archetype: A city-owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers and about 2,750 km of overhead line over a mixed urban, suburban and rural territory.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019-2022, before satellite-based risk planning was piloted in 2022. Trimming is done by contracted utility arborist crews on time-and-material or unit-price contracts; coordinators use GIS maps, spreadsheets and email to plan and track the work and approve invoices in the ERP.

unit_of_work: one circuit-kilometre trimmed on cycle, or one urgent tree request between cycles
trigger: A circuit section comes due in the two- or three-year trimming cycle, or an inspector or customer reports a tree close to or touching a primary line.
end_state: The trees are trimmed to clearance and recorded, the contractor's invoice is approved for payment, or the customer is told that the tree or service wire is theirs to manage.

volume.seasonality: Cycle trimming runs all year, heavier from October to April when leaves are off and bird nesting rules do not restrict work; urgent requests peak in summer growth and after wind and ice storms.

evidence.note: Two-year urban and three-year rural cycles (tdw2026) over about 2,746 km of overhead line (organisation file) give about 1,000 to 1,100 km a year, or 85 to 95 km a month; more than 60,000 trees a year (ho_grids2024) is about 55 to 60 trees per km. About 40 urgent requests a month from inspections and customer calls is the author's estimate. The organisation file's 75 a month counts cycle km only and sits a little low for these cycles.

surge.cause: major storm (wind, ice storm, tornado or derecho)

evidence.note: The May 2022 derecho put more than 180,000 customers out and compressed about four years of emergency repairs into 14 days (source); frequency and multiplier for urgent tree work are the author's estimates.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Three coordinators who also act as forestry inspectors (the utility's own web page refers to forestry inspectors). All three work full time on this process and the steps still imply slightly more than three FTE, which suggests the organisation file is one or two people short or that contractor pre-planners do part of the patrol and notification.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Approves invoices above the coordinator's authority and settles escalated owner disputes.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Not in the process map's roles; places and removes reclose blocks (hold-offs) for contractor crews working close to primary lines.

systems.name: Geographic information system (asset and network model)
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
SCADA for stations and feeder devices

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Pick the next work from the cycle plan or request queue
steps.description: The coordinator reviews the cycle plan spreadsheet for circuits coming due and the queue of tree findings from inspectors and customer service requests, and decides whether each item is cycle work or needs an urgent visit.

evidence.note: Fixed two- and three-year cycles and patrol-based planning from tdw2026; customer requests by phone or service request from ho_veg; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Patrol the circuit before trimming
steps.description: The coordinator drives and walks the circuit section with GIS maps, marks spans that need trimming or removals, notes hazard trees, access problems, gardens and properties that need personal contact, and estimates crew time.

error.defect_description: A span or hazard tree is missed or crew time is underestimated.

evidence.note: Ground patrols as the planning basis before 2022 from the source; time per km is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the work package
steps.description: The coordinator turns the patrol notes into a work package for the contractor: span list, clearances by voltage, removals, spans needing a reclose block or outage, access notes and an estimate, and issues it as a release under the trimming contract.

evidence.note: Clearance of at least 3 m around primary lines (ho_veg) and more for higher voltages (ho_grid2024); package content is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Notify property owners
steps.description: The coordinator or a contractor's notifier leaves door hangers or letters at every affected property giving the dates and work, and phones or visits owners where a tree is to be removed or heavily cut.

control.basis: Property owner notification before planned trimming (utility vegetation management policy)

evidence.note: Notice in person, by phone or letter for planned removals is the practice of a neighbouring Ontario distributor; door hangers and timing are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait out the notice period
steps.description: Owners have about one to two weeks to call with questions or objections before the crew arrives; most do not respond.

next.condition: owner objects or asks for changes

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve an owner's objection
steps.description: The coordinator calls or meets the owner, explains the clearance needed and the outage risk, agrees on a pruning approach or a removal with replacement planting where policy allows, and records any span deferred or escalated.

evidence.note: Working with objecting owners from the source; time and share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Contractor schedules a crew
steps.description: The contractor's general foreman fits the package into the crew schedule, which competes with storm work, other utilities' work and its own staffing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Place a reclose block on the feeder
steps.description: When a crew will work within the limits of approach, its foreman calls the control room and the operator disables automatic reclosing on the feeder in SCADA, logs the hold-off, and removes it when the crew reports clear.

control.basis: Reclose blocking for work near energized lines under the utility's work protection code and IHSA Electrical Utility Safety Rules

evidence.note: Standard Ontario practice; not confirmed in an opened source.

steps.name: Crew mobilizes, weather permitting
steps.description: The crew moves its bucket truck and chipper to the circuit; high wind, lightning, ice and extreme heat stop aerial tree work, so starts slip day by day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Contractor trims the kilometre
steps.description: A three-person utility arborist crew with a bucket truck and chipper prunes the marked trees to clearance, removes hazard trees, chips small branches and leaves cut wood in place where agreed; an urban kilometre with about 55 to 60 trees takes one to three crew days.

error.defect_description: Spans skipped or trimmed short of clearance.

control.basis: Limits of approach for tree work near energized conductors (Ontario Regulation 213/91, Construction Projects)

evidence.note: Trees per km derived from more than 60,000 trees a year (ho_grids2024); clean-up practice from hydroone_veg; crew days are the author's estimate; contractor labour is not this organisation's staff, so it is in the wait.

steps.name: Contractor reports completion
steps.description: The contractor sends the completed span list, timesheets and equipment hours for the package by email, usually with the weekly or monthly billing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Audit the completed work
steps.description: The coordinator drives a sample of the circuit, checks clearances and clean-up against the package, and lists spans that were missed or left short of clearance.

error.defect_description: Sample misses a defective span, which surfaces later as a tree outage.

control.basis: Verification of contractor work before payment (utility contract management policy)

evidence.note: Contractor work verified by small field samples before 2022 (source); times and failure share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Contractor returns to fix missed spans
steps.description: The contractor sends a crew back at its own cost to finish the spans listed in the audit, then emails the coordinator that they are done.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the trimming records
steps.description: The coordinator records the trim date, spans done, removals and deferred spans for the circuit in the GIS layer and the cycle spreadsheet so the next cycle and urgent calls can be checked against it.

error.defect_description: Deferred spans not recorded, so they are missed until the next cycle.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check and approve the invoice
steps.description: The coordinator matches the contractor's invoice lines to timesheets, equipment hours, unit counts and the purchase order release, queries differences with the contractor and approves it in the ERP up to their limit.

error.defect_description: Hours or units billed that were not worked are approved.

control.basis: Receipt and approval of contractor work by the work owner before accounts payable pays (delegated authority policy)

evidence.note: Monthly billing and approval limits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Supervisor approves the invoice
steps.description: The field services supervisor reviews the coordinator's reconciliation of timesheets and units for larger invoices and approves them in the ERP or sends questions back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the invoice to accounts payable
steps.description: The ERP moves the approved invoice into the next payment run and charges the cost to the vegetation management budget.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess the urgent request on site
steps.description: The coordinator looks up the location in the GIS, checks the last trim date, and visits the site to see whether a tree is touching or close to a primary line, is a dead or leaning hazard tree, or only affects the customer's own service wire.

next.condition: customer's service wire or private tree away from primary

evidence.note: Utility trims trees touching or within 3 m of a primary line; customers manage vegetation around their service wires (source); shares and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Explain the customer's responsibility
steps.description: The coordinator calls or emails the customer to explain that the tree or service wire is theirs to manage, and how to book a temporary disconnect so their own arborist can work safely.

evidence.note: Customer responsibility and temporary outage requests from the source.

steps.name: Issue an urgent work order to the contractor
steps.description: The coordinator phones the contractor's on-call foreman and emails a short work order with the location, photos and the work needed, flagged for completion within days.

next.condition: crew must work close to the line

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Place a reclose block for the urgent trim
steps.description: The control room operator disables reclosing on the feeder while the crew works close to the line and restores it when the crew reports clear.

control.basis: Reclose blocking for work near energized lines under the utility's work protection code

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Contractor carries out the urgent trim
steps.description: A contractor crew trims or removes the tree within days, or the same day if it is touching the line, and reports completion with photos.

control.basis: Limits of approach for tree work near energized conductors (Ontario Regulation 213/91, Construction Projects)

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Owner objection
exceptions.description: An owner objects to pruning or removal; the coordinator negotiates and some spans are deferred to the next cycle.

exceptions.name: Missed spans
exceptions.description: The audit finds spans skipped or short of clearance and the contractor returns.

exceptions.name: Customer's own tree
exceptions.description: The urgent request concerns a service wire or private tree, which is the customer's responsibility.

evidence.note: Stated in the source.
More than 60,000 a year in 2024-2025 sources; assumed similar in 2019-2022.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from picking the work to invoice approved (cycle work) or reply or invoice (urgent requests)

evidence.note: Patrol one to four weeks ahead, one to two weeks' notice, one to four weeks for a crew, then audit and monthly billing. Not measured.

pain_points.description: Planning rests on subjective ground patrols and fixed cycles, so effort goes to circuits on the calendar rather than the spans most likely to cause outages.

evidence.note: The source describes this as the reason for moving to remote sensing.

pain_points.description: Audits check only a sample of the work, so missed spans show up later as tree outages.

evidence.note: Small field samples from the source; the consequence is the author's inference.

pain_points.description: Notice periods, owner objections and contractor crew availability stretch each package over weeks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Invoices are matched by hand against timesheets and unit counts in spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: The Trees Are Winning: Hydro Ottawa Is Using Remote Sensing to Fight Back (A. Kemp)
sources.supports: Before the 2022 pilot Hydro Ottawa trimmed on fixed cycles under OEB direction, rural circuits every three years and urban circuits every two; planning relied on ground patrols and outage history; contractor work was verified with small field samples; the May 2022 derecho put more than 180,000 customers out and compressed about four years of emergency repairs into 14 days.

sources.title: With great grids comes great reliability
sources.supports: All 49,000 poles are inspected at 10-year intervals; 38,946 transformers are regularly inspected; crews trim more than 60,000 trees in a typical year; customers get 24 to 72 hours notice of planned outages, with letters for outages over six hours.

sources.title: Vegetation management
sources.supports: Program trims more than 60,000 trees a year; standard is at least 3 metres (10 feet) of clearance around primary lines; customers are responsible for vegetation around their service wires; safety issues and forestry requests come in by phone or a non-electrical service request; forestry inspectors monitor vegetation near lines.

sources.title: An in-depth look at Hydro Ottawa's grid maintenance
sources.supports: Routine inspections of transformers, switches and breakers follow a three-year cycle across the service territory; a critical pole program tests thousands of poles a year; maintenance holes are graded A to E; work often needs the area de-energized, which may need a planned outage; vegetation management units are on two- or three-year cycles; satellite imaging twice a year (introduced after the reference period).

sources.title: Vegetation management practices
sources.supports: A neighbouring Ontario distributor notifies owners in person, by phone, text or letter for planned tree removal, works with owners who object, leaves body wood cut to length in manicured areas and removes small branches, and uses herbicides only with landowner consent.

assumptions: A case is either one circuit-kilometre of cycle trimming (about 68% of cases) or one urgent tree request between cycles (about 32%), so volume is higher than the organisation file's km-only figure.
Coordinator hands-on time implies about 3.5 FTE against three people in the organisation file; the gap is left as found rather than hidden by shortening steps.

Contractor crew time (about one to three three-person crew days per urban km) sits in the wait times of external steps, because those crews are not the organisation's staff; the staffing check therefore covers only coordinators, the supervisor and control room operators.
The cycle plan is treated as a trigger from the capital plan; the process map lists only inspection findings and customer inquiries as triggers.
Patrol-based planning, fixed cycles and sample audits describe 2019-2022; satellite and AI-based planning began as a pilot in 2022 and is not modelled.
Reclose blocks are placed for about half of the work; the share is an estimate.
Storm clean-up of trees during a major event is run by the storm response process; the surge here is the extra urgent and follow-up trimming in the weeks after.
